For the last few years I've built autonomous delivery systems — the agents, pipelines and review bots that let a team ship without doing everything by hand. I work directly with founders and engineering leaders, usually solo, and I hand everything over so your team owns it. Open to project work, retainers, an occasional fractional or advisory seat — or a full-time lead role for the right team.

underHood.heading: How the pipeline actually works
underHood.subtitle: The short version of what I build — and, just as important, how it behaves when something goes wrong.

1.d: An agent turns a ticket or spec into a concrete, reviewable plan.

2.d: It implements the change in small, isolated commits on its own branch.

3.d: A separate agent reviews the diff for bugs, security and your conventions.

4.d: A PR only opens once tests pass and the change matches what the ticket asked.

5.d: A human approves. Deploy and preview then happen automatically.

6.d: Production is monitored, and anything off triggers a rollback.

underHood.failureBody: It does sometimes, and that's the part I design for. Flaky tests get retried and quarantined, not merged around. A failed build blocks the PR, never the pipeline. Review false-positives are cheap to dismiss and get fed back so the agent stops repeating them. And because every change is a small, reversible commit behind a human approval, a bad one costs you a single revert, not an outage. On one platform a bad autonomous change slipped a regression into staging — the watch caught it, rolled it back on its own, and it never reached a user.

whoFor.heading: Where this fits, and where it doesn't
whoFor.enterprise: Larger or regulated org? I don't do SOC 2 or enterprise procurement — but I do advise internal AI-delivery teams and run contained single-team pilots under NDA. Worth a conversation.

for.1: A team of 3 to ~100 engineers that ships too slowly
for.2: A founder or eng leader who wants delivery automated, not outsourced
for.3: On modern tooling (Git, CI, containers) — SaaS, fintech, e-commerce, marketplaces
for.4: Happy to keep a human approving what ships

not.1: A large enterprise that needs a vendor with SOC 2, procurement and an MSA — I'm a solo operator
not.2: Looking to hand over control entirely, with no human in the loop

1.q: Is it just you? What if you're unavailable?
1.a: Yes, you work directly with me, no rotating team. I keep a short bench of trusted engineers I can pull in for capacity, I document everything as I go (runbooks included), and I hand it all over so your team can run it without me. Nothing depends on me being around.

2.q: Can I talk to a past client?
2.a: Yes. I'll connect you with a reference on our call. I keep client names off a public page out of respect, not because they aren't real.

3.q: Do you work in regulated or compliance-heavy environments?
3.a: It's built for it. Everything runs self-hosted in your environment, and the agents work on your code in CI, not your production data. Nothing has to leave your infrastructure — I can run on self-hosted or local models so no code or logs go to a third party. Every agent action is logged for audit, access is least-privilege with rotated secrets, and I'll sign an NDA, DPA or BAA and work to your security rules. If you need a vendor with formal SOC 2 or HITRUST certification, I'm honestly not your fit.

4.q: Will it work with our stack?
4.a: If you're on Git with some form of CI and containers, yes. I meet your setup where it is instead of forcing a new one.

5.a: On the team's own repos, comparing the weeks before and after the automation went live. I'll walk you through the exact baseline on a call — I'd rather show you the method than ask you to trust a headline.

6.q: Can you deliver under my agency's brand?
6.a: Yes. I subcontract white-label for agencies, work in front of your clients as part of your team, and upskill your engineers so you can carry it forward.

7.q: I'm a small, budget-tight team. Is this for me?
7.a: Very likely yes — small teams feel the pain most. If you're not sure, start with a free 20-minute diagnostic, no pitch. And the Audit ships one working automation, so you see real value before committing to anything bigger.

8.q: Are you open to a fractional or full-time role?
8.a: Yes. Alongside project work I take fractional and advisory seats, and for the right team I'd consider a full-time Staff/lead role owning delivery automation and mentoring the team. Happy to talk comp and scope directly.

usage-agent.name: Product Copilot
usage-agent.subtitle: Answers users' questions inside your app
usage-agent.overview: A RAG-powered conversational agent that helps end-users navigate a modular multi-tenant SaaS platform. The agent answers product questions, guides users to the right screens and menus, and explains features without technical jargon. Built to reduce support burden by grounding every answer in the actual knowledge base: specs, UI flows, domain documentation.

steps.1: Receives a user question in natural language (French-first)
steps.2: Searches knowledge base with multi-step RAG (specs, domain, backend, frontend collections)
steps.3: Constructs a contextual, jargon-free answer with source grounding
steps.4: Returns a guided response pointing to the right screen or procedure

capabilities.1: Multi-collection RAG search across specs, domain, backend and frontend documents
capabilities.2: French-first responses with clear, non-technical language
capabilities.3: Guided navigation answers pointing to exact UI locations
capabilities.4: Context-aware follow-ups using LangChain agent memory
capabilities.5: Pluggable knowledge base via Chroma DB vector embeddings

spec-agent.name: Spec Architect
spec-agent.subtitle: Turns a business need into ready-to-build specs
spec-agent.overview: An agentic system that transforms a raw business need into two structured markdown specification files: a Domain model (entities, relationships, reused concepts) and a UserStories document (workflows, user scenarios). The agent searches the existing knowledge base to reuse consistent terminology and patterns — eliminating manual spec writing and ensuring every new feature aligns with the established architecture.

steps.1: Takes a business need description as free-form text input
steps.2: Searches existing specs for similar feature structures
steps.3: Searches domain models for reusable entities and relationships
steps.4: Searches backend and frontend patterns for architectural conventions
steps.5: Generates Domain.md with entity definitions and UserStories.md with workflows
steps.6: Writes both markdown files to the target directory

capabilities.1: Generates Domain.md with entities, attributes and relationships
capabilities.2: Generates UserStories.md with structured scenarios and workflows
capabilities.3: Reuses existing terminology from the knowledge base for consistency
capabilities.4: Multi-step RAG retrieval across four document collections
capabilities.5: Write-to-disk capability via markdown file tool

sql-agent.name: Data Analyst
sql-agent.subtitle: Ask your database in plain language
sql-agent.overview: A safety-first agent that allows non-technical team members to query live business data using plain English or French. The agent inspects the database schema before every query, writes read-only SQL, executes it, and returns the results as a clear natural language answer. Strict guardrails enforce that only SELECT and WITH statements are executed — no mutations ever reach the database.

steps.1: Receives a natural language question about business data
steps.2: Inspects the full database schema to understand available tables and columns
steps.3: Writes a targeted read-only SQL query (SELECT or WITH only)
steps.4: Executes the query against the database (SQLite or MariaDB)
steps.5: Translates the result rows into a clear natural language answer

capabilities.1: Schema-first workflow: always inspects structure before writing SQL
capabilities.2: Read-only enforcement: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP are blocked at system prompt level
capabilities.3: Supports both SQLite and MariaDB backends via SqlBackend interface
capabilities.4: Returns structured results with row count and column context
capabilities.5: Handles multi-table questions with JOIN and aggregation

orchestrator-agent.name: AI Concierge
orchestrator-agent.subtitle: Routes every request to the right specialist
orchestrator-agent.overview: A high-level routing agent that serves as a single entry point for all platform questions. It classifies the incoming question and delegates to the appropriate specialist: the SQL Agent for data and statistics queries, and the Usage Agent for product navigation and procedural help. Users never need to know which agent to call — the Orchestrator decides and returns a unified answer in French.

steps.1: Receives any user question as input
steps.2: Classifies the question: data/statistics vs. product navigation/procedure
steps.3: Delegates to SQL Agent for counts, reports, or database content questions
steps.4: Delegates to Usage Agent for how-to, navigation, and feature questions
steps.5: Returns a unified, contextual answer in French

capabilities.1: Single entry point for both data and product questions
capabilities.2: Intelligent routing based on question semantics
capabilities.3: Wraps specialist agents as callable tools
capabilities.5: Extensible: new agents can be added as additional tools

brick-generator.name: Feature Builder
brick-generator.subtitle: Generates full-stack features from a spec
brick-generator.overview: The most complex agent in the suite. Given a Domain spec and UserStories file, it autonomously generates a complete production-ready feature module — full-stack, with NestJS backend files and Nuxt/Vue frontend files — following the target application's exact architectural conventions. Sub-agents handle backend and frontend generation separately, then all files are written, integrated into the monorepo, and validated automatically.

steps.1: Reads the Domain.md and UserStories.md spec files
steps.2: Reads the target application's structure and architectural conventions
steps.3: Searches reference codebases for backend patterns (NestJS modules, DTOs, services)
steps.4: Sub-agent generates all backend files following found patterns
steps.5: Searches reference codebases for frontend patterns (Nuxt pages, components, composables)
steps.6: Sub-agent generates all frontend files following found patterns
steps.7: Merges backend + frontend files and writes them to the target application
steps.8: Runs integration to register the new module in parent configs
steps.9: Validates all required files exist and fixes any missing ones

capabilities.1: Generates complete NestJS modules: controllers, services, DTOs, entities, guards
capabilities.2: Generates complete Nuxt apps: pages, components, composables, stores, i18n
capabilities.3: Pattern-aware generation via RAG search on reference codebases
capabilities.4: Automatic monorepo integration (registers the module in all parent configs)
capabilities.5: Self-validating: detects and fixes missing files after generation
capabilities.6: Sub-agent architecture separates concerns (backend vs. frontend generation)
